scheme_name: Subsidy Scheme For Establishment Of Goat Unit (10+1) For Scheduled Tribe Women
description:
The Subsidy Scheme for Establishment of Goat Unit (10+1) for Scheduled Tribe Women was launched by the Government of India in 2014. 

This scheme aims to empower Scheduled Tribe women by providing them with financial assistance to establish goat farming units. 

The initiative is part of the broader objective to enhance the livelihood opportunities for women belonging to Scheduled Tribes. 

The scheme specifically targets women who are members of Scheduled Tribes and aims to improve their socio-economic status. 

The primary objective of the scheme is to provide financial support for the establishment of a goat unit consisting of ten female goats and one male goat. 

The scheme aims to promote self-employment among Scheduled Tribe women. 

It also seeks to enhance the income levels of these women through goat rearing. 

The financial assistance provided under the scheme is intended to cover the initial costs associated with establishing the goat unit. 

The total subsidy amount provided under the scheme is INR 1.5 lakh. 

This amount is intended to cover the costs of purchasing goats, constructing shelters, and other necessary expenses related to goat farming. 

The subsidy is provided at a rate of 50 percent of the total project cost. 

For women belonging to Scheduled Tribes, the maximum subsidy amount is capped at INR 75,000. 

The scheme is designed to benefit approximately 10,000 Scheduled Tribe women across various states in India. 

Eligible beneficiaries must be at least 18 years old and should not exceed 55 years of age. 

They must belong to a Scheduled Tribe as recognized by the Government of India. 

The income limit for eligibility is set at INR 1 lakh per annum for the family. 

Applicants must have a basic understanding of goat rearing practices. 

They should also possess the necessary skills to manage a goat unit effectively. 

The application process for the scheme involves several steps. 

Interested applicants must first obtain an application form from the local office of the Department of Animal Husbandry. 

The application form can also be downloaded from the official website of the Ministry of Animal Husbandry, Dairying and Fisheries. 

Applicants are required to submit the completed application form along with relevant documents. 

These documents include proof of Scheduled Tribe status, income certificate, and identity proof. 

The application must also include a project report detailing the proposed goat unit. 

Once the application is submitted, it will be reviewed by the local authorities. 

The review process typically takes about 30 days. 

If approved, the subsidy amount will be disbursed directly to the beneficiary's bank account. 

The disbursement of funds is usually completed within 15 days of approval. 

Beneficiaries are expected to utilize the funds for the specific purposes outlined in their project report. 

The scheme also includes provisions for training and capacity building. 

Beneficiaries will receive training on goat rearing and management practices. 

This training is conducted by the Department of Animal Husbandry in collaboration with various NGOs. 

The training program typically lasts for about 10 days. 

It covers essential topics such as feeding, health care, and breeding of goats. 

The goat units established under this scheme are expected to generate a sustainable income for the beneficiaries. 

On average, a goat can produce 1 to 2 kids annually. 

The sale of goats and goat products can significantly enhance the income of the beneficiaries. 

The scheme is implemented by the Department of Animal Husbandry under the Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying. 

The contact details for the Department of Animal Husbandry can be found on the official website of the ministry. 

The scheme has been positively received in various states, with many women reporting increased income levels. 

The government aims to expand the reach of this scheme to cover more beneficiaries in the coming years. 

The success of the scheme is measured by the number of goat units established and the income generated by the beneficiaries. 

Regular monitoring and evaluation are conducted to assess the impact of the scheme. 

The government has set a target to establish at least 5,000 goat units by the end of the financial year 2024. 

The scheme is part of the National Livestock Mission, which aims to promote sustainable livestock development. 

The government is committed to enhancing the livelihoods of marginalized communities through various welfare schemes. 

The Subsidy Scheme for Establishment of Goat Unit (10+1) for Scheduled Tribe Women is a significant step towards achieving this goal. 

By providing financial assistance and training, the scheme empowers women to become self-reliant. 

The initiative also contributes to the overall economic development of rural areas. 

The government encourages more women to participate in this scheme to uplift their families and communities. 

The scheme is expected to create a ripple effect in the local economy by increasing the demand for goat products. 

The establishment of goat units can lead to job creation in related sectors such as feed supply and veterinary services. 

Overall, the Subsidy Scheme for Establishment of Goat Unit (10+1) for Scheduled Tribe Women is a comprehensive initiative aimed at promoting self-employment and economic empowerment. 

The scheme not only benefits individual women but also contributes to the development of the entire community. 

With continued support and proper implementation, the scheme has the potential to transform the lives of many Scheduled Tribe women across India. 

The government remains committed to ensuring that the benefits of this scheme reach the intended beneficiaries effectively. 

Through this initiative, the government aims to create a more equitable society where women have equal opportunities for growth and development. 

The Subsidy Scheme for Establishment of Goat Unit (10+1) for Scheduled Tribe Women serves as a model for similar initiatives aimed at empowering marginalized communities. 

The success of this scheme can inspire other states to implement similar programs for different livestock and agricultural activities. 

In conclusion, this scheme represents a significant effort by the Indian government to uplift Scheduled Tribe women and enhance their livelihoods through sustainable practices.
